title: Drag appears only when a solid touches a moving fluid
summary: Drag is a mechanical force from touching air or another fluid, and it points against the aircraft's motion.
body: NASA Glenn defines drag as the aerodynamic force that opposes an aircraft's motion through the air, including drag from the engines. It is generated by contact between a solid and a fluid, liquid or gas. Unlike a gravitational field, it cannot act across empty space. With no fluid around the body, that force is absent. The arrow of the force is opposite the motion. Page last updated 21 July 2022.

sources.title: What is Drag?
sources.author: Nancy Hall, NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.note: Public-domain NASA Glenn page, last updated 21 July 2022. Paraphrase of the definition: drag opposes motion, requires contact with a fluid, and requires relative motion.
